statements.notes: Purpose statement: the stage output is an explicit, numbered requirement set that the patch must satisfy.
statements.quote: Convert the task description into an explicit, numbered set of requirements that the patch must satisfy

statements.notes: The stage artifact must exist at this exact path.
statements.quote: **Artifact**: `/tmp/swe-bench-pro/02-requirements-analysis.md`

statements.notes: Prerequisite: the Stage 1 artifact must exist and record Affected Scope, Build & Test Commands, Existing Tests, and Baseline before Stage 2 starts.
statements.quote: Reverse Engineering is complete: its Affected Scope, Build & Test Commands, Existing Tests, and Baseline are established, and recorded in `/tmp/swe-bench-pro/01-reverse-engineering.md`

statements.notes: Requirements Analysis comes after Reverse Engineering is complete (the 01 artifact predates the 02 artifact).
statements.quote: Reverse Engineering is complete

statements.notes: Named symbols, signatures, and file paths from the task description must be used as given.
statements.quote: Treat everything the task description states as authoritative — expected behavior, named symbols, signatures, file paths

statements.notes: Requirements must not paraphrase or re-derive content the task description already specifies.
statements.quote: Do not re-derive or reword what is already specified

statements.notes: The Stage 1 artifact should be read and used to map behavior onto code and onto existing test contracts.
statements.quote: Use the Reverse Engineering result as context for how the described behavior maps onto actual code and onto the contract enforced by existing tests

statements.notes: One statement per requirement; no compound requirements.
statements.quote: **MANDATORY**: Express every requirement as a single, verifiable statement

statements.notes: Requirement IDs must follow the pattern R<number>.
statements.quote: identified as `R1`, `R2`, `R3`, and so on

statements.notes: Defines verifiability: each requirement must be checkable by a reproduction script or by existing tests.
statements.quote: A requirement is verifiable when it can be checked either by running a reproduction script or by running existing tests.

statements.notes: Requirements that cannot be verified must not be included.
statements.quote: A requirement that cannot be checked by either means is out of scope.

statements.notes: Numbering runs continuously across Functional, Non-Functional, and Edge Cases; it does not restart in each section.
statements.quote: Number the requirements in one sequence across all three categories

statements.notes: No duplicate Rn IDs in the artifact; the IDs are referenced by later stages.
statements.quote: so that each identifier is unique in the artifact and can be traced from Stage 3 onward

statements.notes: All three categories must be considered; heading presence is checkable.
statements.quote: Evaluate all three categories:

statements.notes: Functional Requirements must cover the behavior after the fix.
statements.quote: The behavior the affected code must exhibit once the issue is resolved

statements.notes: Functional Requirements must also cover preserved behavior, i.e. the contracts enforced by existing tests.
statements.quote: The behavior it must continue to exhibit — contracts visible in existing tests that the change must not break

statements.notes: Defines what belongs under Non-Functional Requirements.
statements.quote: Constraints on how the behavior must be achieved — complexity or memory bounds

statements.notes: Non-functional requirements not stated in the task description must not be invented.
statements.quote: Only what the task description states; often nothing

statements.notes: The skeleton says to write "none stated" under an Rn item when the task description gives no NFRs; the section must not be left empty or dropped.
statements.quote: often nothing

statements.notes: Edge-case categories that should be evaluated.
statements.quote: Boundary values, empty and null inputs, invalid inputs, and type or range limits

statements.notes: Each error path must say whether it raises or is handled, plus the observable result; the skeleton format is 'condition -> expected behavior'.
statements.quote: Error paths: which condition must raise, which must be handled, and what the observable result is

statements.notes: The artifact file must be written.
statements.quote: Write `/tmp/swe-bench-pro/02-requirements-analysis.md`

statements.notes: Write the full content in one operation, with no incremental edits; this is hard to check from the artifact alone.
statements.quote: in a single write, with the full content below

statements.notes: The skeleton frontmatter has keys stage and name, with values 2 and requirements-analysis.
statements.quote: Keep the frontmatter keys ... exactly as given.

statements.notes: Heading text must match the skeleton exactly.
statements.quote: Keep ... the `##` headings ... exactly as given.
statements.target: ## Functional Requirements, ## Non-Functional Requirements, ## Edge Cases & Error Handling, ## Assumptions

statements.notes: Each requirement line must start with '- R<number>:'.
statements.quote: Keep ... the `- Rn:` prefix exactly as given.

statements.notes: All bracketed placeholders, e.g. [statement] or [condition -> expected behavior], must be replaced; no unreplaced placeholders may remain.
statements.quote: Replace only the bracketed text.

statements.notes: Every heading must be present even if its category has no content.
statements.quote: A dropped heading reads as an unevaluated category.

statements.notes: Completion criterion: numbering and uniqueness can be checked; verifiability cannot.
statements.quote: Every requirement stated as a numbered, verifiable item, uniquely identified across all categories

statements.notes: Completion criterion: all three category headings must be present.
statements.quote: All three categories evaluated, each with its heading present
statements.target: ## Functional Requirements, ## Non-Functional Requirements, ## Edge Cases & Error Handling

statements.notes: Each assumption should give the ambiguity, the decision, and the reasoning; the heading's presence is checkable.
statements.quote: Assumptions made in place of clarifying questions recorded explicitly

statements.notes: Implies the agent resolves ambiguity by making a recorded decision instead of asking the user clarifying questions.
statements.quote: Assumptions made in place of clarifying questions

statements.notes: Completion criterion: the artifact must follow the skeleton structure (frontmatter, four headings, Rn items).
statements.quote: `/tmp/swe-bench-pro/02-requirements-analysis.md` written in the prescribed skeleton
